assumptions.choice: Feed is fixed at 1h bars by the harness; 4h candles are built manually by accumulating bars and finalizing when hour%4==3, so an entry order placed on that bar fills at the next bar's open, which is the true open of the next 4h candle.
assumptions.reason: Spec requires a 4h timeframe but the environment only provides 1h bars; this reconstruction is the closest literal reading.

assumptions.choice: 4h period boundaries are derived from each bar's own clock hour rather than counting bars, so occasional trading-hour gaps only shorten a period instead of desynchronizing later ones.
assumptions.reason: Futures data can have small session gaps; hour-based boundaries are self-correcting without needing special gap handling.

assumptions.choice: Symmetric fractal: a bar is a local high/low if it is the max/min within a window of N bars on each side (N=7), confirmed once N bars afterward are available.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'based on the last N candles' but does not define the exact algorithm; symmetric fractal confirmation is the standard technique for this description and N=7 sits in the stated 5-10 range.

assumptions.choice: A trendline is 'active' if the breakout close occurs within M=10 bars of the line's second (most recent) defining point; once any close occurs beyond the line, it is marked broken and cannot fire again.
assumptions.reason: Spec defines 'active' only informally ('not broken during the last M candles'); this operationalizes it as an expiry window plus single-fire breakout.

assumptions.choice: Used the local-low/high-based stop (entry trendline's most recent point) rather than the alternate fixed-distance-from-breakout method, with a buffer of 12 points reused from the spec's 10-15 point example.
assumptions.reason: Spec offers two alternative stop placements ('or'); one had to be chosen, and the local-extremum method is listed first and ties naturally to the trendline construction.

assumptions.choice: Size = (risk_pct * equity) / risk_points, treating 1 price point as $1 of P&L per unit (no futures point multiplier applied).
assumptions.reason: The harness's broker/data feed do not configure a futures contract multiplier, so backtrader's default stock-style P&L accounting is the only mechanism available for size calculation.

assumptions.choice: ATR is computed manually as the simple arithmetic mean of True Range over the manually-aggregated 4h bars (not Wilder-smoothed, not bt.indicators.ATR).
assumptions.reason: bt.indicators.ATR only operates on the native 1h feed; since 4h bars are built manually, the ATR filter must also be computed manually on that series.

assumptions.choice: Treated as a required entry gate (breakout candle volume must exceed the average of the prior 10 4h candles), not merely optional confirmation.
assumptions.reason: Unlike the trend filter, the spec does not label the volume filter 'optional', so it is implemented as a hard condition.

assumptions.choice: The optional higher-timeframe (daily) trend filter is omitted entirely.
assumptions.reason: Only one 1h data feed is available in this environment and the spec explicitly marks this filter optional.

assumptions.choice: Take-profit and stop-loss are implemented as a manual OCO bracket (separate Stop and Limit orders submitted after entry fill; whichever fills first cancels the other).
assumptions.reason: Spec requires both a fixed 1:2 R:R take-profit and a stop-loss that can trail, which requires independently modifiable stop/limit orders rather than a single bracket call.

assumptions.choice: Stop is only re-evaluated for trailing when a new confirmed local low/high (per the N-bar fractal) forms while in position, and only moved in the favorable direction; the take-profit level itself is never trailed.
assumptions.reason: Spec ties the trailing stop explicitly to newly formed local extrema, and only describes moving the stop, not the target.

assumptions.choice: ATR filter passes automatically until 50 4h bars of True Range history exist; volume filter passes automatically until 10 prior 4h bars exist; trendlines/extrema simply do not exist until enough bars accumulate.
assumptions.reason: No manual bar-skipping is specified; relying on natural data availability mirrors backtrader's automatic minperiod behavior for this manually-computed series.
